why: Level by level, left to right is exactly breadth-first search on the tree, where you process the queue one whole level at a time.
hints: Depth-first traversal does not visit nodes in level order. Which traversal visits all nodes at depth d before any at depth d+1?
BFS with a queue. At the start of each round, the queue holds exactly one level; record its length and pop that many nodes.
Collect each level's values into a list, enqueue left then right children. O(n) time, O(width) space.
pitfalls: Take len(queue) before the inner loop; it changes as you add children.
